title: What every living thing does
stem: Which of these is true of every living thing?
key: Every living thing needs water, food and air, grows, responds and reproduces.

options.text: It moves from place to place.
options.pick: Animals move about, so living things seem to move.
options.why: Plants are living but stay in one place.

options.pick: Many animals make sounds.
options.why: Plants and fish are living but make no sounds we can hear.

options.pick: Which one is true of plants and animals alike?
options.why: Every living thing grows: a chick into a hen, a seed into a plant.

options.pick: Most animals we know have legs.
options.why: Snakes, fish and plants have no legs, but they are living.

title: A seed and a pebble
stem:
Ali put a bean seed and a pebble on wet cotton wool. The table shows what he saw.

What does this show?
figure:
DayBean seedPebble
0no changeno change
5has a root and a shootno change
key: A seed is living: it grows when it gets water.

options.text: Seeds are not living until they are planted in soil.
options.pick: A seed looks hard and still, like a pebble.
options.why: The seed grew on cotton wool, without soil. It is living.

options.text: The pebble is living, because it sat in water too.
options.pick: It had the same water as the seed.
options.why: The pebble did not grow or change. It is not living.

options.text: The seed is living, because it grew when it had water.
options.pick: Which one showed a characteristic of living things?
options.why: The seed grew a root and a shoot. Growing shows it is living.

options.text: Both are not living, because neither moved.
options.pick: Living things seem to move.
options.why: Moving is not what tells us. The seed grew, so it is living.

title: A plant at the window
stem:
A potted plant on a windowsill slowly bends towards the light.

Which characteristic of living things does this show?
key: Reacting to a change, such as light, is responding.

options.text: It responds to changes around it.
options.pick: Is the plant getting bigger, or reacting to something?
options.why: The plant reacts to where the light is coming from: it responds.

options.pick: Bending seems to be a kind of growing.
options.why: The bending is a reaction to light. That is responding.

options.pick: Something is changing, and reproducing is a change.
options.why: Reproducing means making young. No new plant is made here.

options.text: It moves from place to place.
options.pick: The plant is moving.
options.why: It stays in its pot. It only turns towards the light.

title: A toy robot dog
stem:
A toy robot dog walks, barks and turns its head when you clap.

Which statement is correct?
key: A living thing does all of these: needs water, food and air, grows, responds and reproduces.

options.text: It is living, because it moves and responds to sound.
options.pick: It does things that animals do.
options.why: A living thing must also need food, water and air, grow and reproduce. The robot does none of these.

options.text: It is living, because it needs batteries the way we need food.
options.pick: Batteries seem like its food.
options.why: It doesn't grow or reproduce, so it is not living.

options.text: Only animals with fur are living, so it is not living.
options.pick: Real dogs have fur.
options.why: Plants, fish and birds are living without fur. The robot is not living because it doesn't grow or reproduce.

options.text: It is not living, because it does not grow, reproduce or need food, water and air.
options.pick: Check every characteristic, not just one.
options.why: Moving and making sounds are not enough. It lacks the other characteristics.

title: A penguin
stem:
A penguin cannot fly, swims in the sea, and has feathers and a beak.

Which group of animals does it belong to?
key: Group animals by body features. Feathers and a beak: bird.

options.text: Fish, because it swims in the sea
options.pick: It lives in water.
options.why: Fish have scales and fins. A penguin has feathers and a beak.

options.text: Birds, because it has feathers and a beak
options.pick: Look at its body, not where it swims.
options.why: Feathers and a beak make it a bird, even though it cannot fly.

options.pick: Birds seem to be the animals that fly.
options.why: Not flying doesn't decide the group. Feathers do.

options.pick: Reptiles lay eggs.
options.why: Birds lay eggs too. Feathers and a beak make it a bird.

title: Which one is an insect?
stem: Which animal is an insect?
key: Insects have 6 legs and 3 body parts. A spider, with 8 legs, is not an insect.

options.text: An animal with 6 legs and 3 body parts
options.pick: Count the legs and the body parts.
options.why: 6 legs and 3 body parts (head, thorax, abdomen) make an insect.

options.text: An animal with 8 legs and 2 body parts
options.pick: It is small and has many legs.
options.why: That is a spider. Insects have 6 legs and 3 body parts.

options.text: An animal with many legs and a long body made of many parts
options.pick: It is a small creeping animal.
options.why: Insects have exactly 6 legs and 3 body parts.

options.text: An animal with a shell and no legs
options.pick: It is small, like many insects.
options.why: Insects have 6 legs.

title: Body coverings
stem:
The table shows the body coverings of four animals, P, Q, R and S.

Which animal could be a frog?
figure:
AnimalBody covering
Pdry, scaly skin
Qmoist, smooth skin
Rfeathers
Sfur
key: Amphibians, such as frogs, have moist, smooth skin.

options.pick: Frogs and lizards look a bit alike.
options.why: Dry, scaly skin belongs to reptiles. A frog's skin is moist and smooth.

options.pick: Picked at random.
options.why: Feathers belong to birds.

options.pick: Many animals are furry.
options.why: Fur belongs to mammals.

options.pick: Which skin do amphibians have?
options.why: Frogs are amphibians, with moist, smooth skin.

title: A mushroom
stem: Which statement about a mushroom is correct?
key: Fungi are not plants: they are not green and cannot make their own food.

options.text: It is a plant, because it grows out of the ground.
options.pick: It grows where plants grow.
options.why: A mushroom is a fungus. It is not green and cannot make its own food.

options.text: It is a fungus. It is not green and cannot make its own food.
options.pick: Is it green? Can it make its own food?
options.why: Mushrooms are fungi, not plants.

options.text: It is not living, because it does not move.
options.pick: It stays in one place, like a stone.
options.why: Mushrooms grow and reproduce, so they are living.

options.text: It is a plant, because it has a stalk.
options.pick: The stalk looks like a stem.
options.why: Having a stalk doesn't make it a plant. It is a fungus.

title: Bacteria
stem: Which statement about bacteria is correct?
key: Bacteria are living things too small to see without a microscope.

options.text: They can be seen easily on dirty hands.
options.pick: Dirt on hands seems to be the bacteria.
options.why: Bacteria are too small to see without a microscope.

options.text: They are not living, because we cannot see them.
options.pick: Things we can't see seem not to be alive.
options.why: Bacteria are living things. They are just very tiny.

options.text: They are a kind of plant.
options.pick: They are not animals, so they seem to be plants.
options.why: Bacteria are a group of their own.

options.text: They are living things that can be seen only through a microscope.
options.pick: How big are bacteria?
options.why: Bacteria are living, and too small to see with the eyes alone.

title: Group Y
stem:
Mei sorted some plants into two groups, X and Y.

Which heading is correct for Group Y?
figure:
GroupPlants
Xhibiscus, sunflower, mango tree
Yfern, moss
key: Non-flowering plants, such as ferns and mosses, never make flowers.

options.pick: Ferns and mosses like damp places.
options.why: Liking damp places isn't a heading here. Both groups grow on land.

options.pick: Ferns and mosses are small.
options.why: Size and stem strength aren't what separates the groups. Flowers are.

options.pick: What do hibiscus, sunflowers and mango trees have that ferns and mosses never have?
options.why: Ferns and mosses never make flowers.

options.pick: They have no flowers, so they seem not to be plants.
options.why: Ferns and mosses are plants that don't flower.

title: Which is living?
stem: Which of these is a living thing?
key: A living thing grows, responds, reproduces and needs water, food and air.

options.text: A toy car that moves on its own
options.pick: It moves by itself.
options.why: It doesn't grow, reproduce or need food, water and air.

options.pick: It grows.
options.why: It gets bigger only because air is blown in. It can't grow by itself.

options.pick: Its hands move.
options.why: Moving isn't enough. It doesn't grow or reproduce.

options.pick: Which one grows and reproduces on its own?
options.why: Mould is a fungus. It grows and spreads, so it is living.

title: A growing balloon
stem:
A balloon gets bigger as air is blown into it.

Is it growing the way a living thing grows?
key: A living thing grows by itself. Getting bigger because something is pushed in is not growing.

options.pick: Getting bigger sounds like growing.
options.why: It gets bigger only because air is pushed in. It cannot grow by itself.

options.text: No. It gets bigger only when air is pushed in. It cannot grow by itself, or reproduce.
options.pick: Would it get bigger on its own?
options.why: A living thing grows by itself. The balloon doesn't.

options.pick: Living things need air.
options.why: Needing air alone doesn't make something living.

options.text: Yes, because it is responding to the air.
options.pick: It changes when air comes in.
options.why: Responding is a living thing reacting to a change. The balloon is only being filled.

title: Is a plant living?
stem: Which shows that a plant is a living thing?
key: Plants grow and reproduce, so they are living.

options.pick: That is something plants do.
options.why: A stone stays in one place too.

options.pick: Plants are green.
options.why: A green ball is not living.

options.pick: Trees are wood.
options.why: A wooden chair is not living.

options.text: It grows and makes new plants.
options.pick: Which characteristics of living things does a plant show?
options.why: Growing and reproducing show that it is living.

title: Do plants need air?
stem:
Siti says plants do not need air, only water.

Which is correct?
key: Plants need water, food and air, like all living things. They make their own food.

options.text: Plants need water, food and air to survive, like all living things.
options.pick: What do all living things need?
options.why: Plants are living, so they need water, food and air. They make their own food.

options.pick: We water plants, but don't feed them.
options.why: Plants also need air, and food, which they make themselves.

options.pick: Plants grow in soil.
options.why: Plants need water, food and air.

options.text: Plants need nothing, because they are not living.
options.pick: Plants don't move or eat like animals.
options.why: Plants are living things.

title: A chick to a hen
stem:
A chick hatches, and some weeks later it has become a hen.

Which characteristic does this show?
key: Getting bigger over time is growing.

options.pick: A hen is a grown-up chick, and hens lay eggs.
options.why: Becoming a hen is getting bigger. That is growing.

options.pick: The chick changes.
options.why: Responding is reacting to something around it.

options.pick: What is changing about the chick?
options.why: The chick gets bigger and becomes a hen: it grows.

options.pick: The chick eats to get bigger.
options.why: It does need food, but the change shown is growing.

title: A snail
stem:
A snail pulls into its shell when it is touched.

Which characteristic does this show?
key: Reacting to a change, such as a touch, is responding.

options.pick: The snail changes shape.
options.why: It doesn't get bigger. It reacts to the touch.

options.text: It responds to changes around it.
options.pick: What makes the snail pull in?
options.why: The snail reacts to the touch: it responds.

options.pick: Snails make young.
options.why: Pulling in is not making young.

options.text: It moves from place to place.
options.pick: The snail moved.
options.why: It pulled into its shell. That is a reaction to the touch.

title: Kittens
stem:
A cat has a litter of kittens.

Which characteristic does this show?
key: Making young of its own kind is reproducing.

options.pick: The kittens will grow.
options.why: The cat making kittens is reproducing.

options.pick: Cats need air.
options.why: True, but it is not what is shown here.

options.pick: The cat looks after its kittens.
options.why: Making young is reproducing.

options.pick: What does making young show?
options.why: Making young of its own kind is reproducing.

title: A bat
stem:
A bat flies with wings, and its body is covered with fur.

Which group does it belong to?
key: Fur or hair: mammal, even if it flies.

options.pick: Flying animals seem to be birds.
options.why: Birds have feathers and beaks. The bat has fur.

options.pick: Insects have wings.
options.why: Insects have 6 legs and 3 body parts.

options.pick: What covers its body?
options.why: Fur makes it a mammal, even though it flies.

options.pick: Bats live in dark caves, like some reptiles.
options.why: Reptiles have dry, scaly skin, not fur.

title: A sea turtle
stem:
A sea turtle lives in the sea and swims with flippers. It has dry, scaly skin and lays its eggs on the beach.

Which group does it belong to?
key: Dry, scaly skin: reptile, even if it lives in the sea.

options.pick: What is its skin like?
options.why: Dry, scaly skin makes it a reptile, even though it lives in the sea.

options.text: Fish, because it lives in the sea
options.pick: It lives in water.
options.why: Fish have fins and scales; the turtle has flippers and dry, scaly skin.

options.text: Amphibians, because it lives in water and on land
options.pick: It goes onto the beach.
options.why: Amphibians have moist, smooth skin.

options.pick: It is a big animal.
options.why: Mammals have fur or hair.

title: Birds' covering
stem: What covers the body of a bird?
key: Feathers cover a bird's body.

options.pick: Birds' legs look scaly.
options.why: A bird's body is covered with feathers.

options.pick: Some birds look fluffy.
options.why: The fluff is feathers.

options.pick: Water birds get wet.
options.why: Moist skin belongs to amphibians.

options.pick: What do all birds have?
options.why: Feathers cover a bird's body.

title: A frog and a lizard
stem: Which statement is correct?
key: Frogs (amphibians) have moist, smooth skin. Lizards (reptiles) have dry, scaly skin.

options.text: A frog has moist, smooth skin, and a lizard has dry, scaly skin.
options.pick: Which one lives near water and feels slippery?
options.why: Frogs are amphibians with moist skin; lizards are reptiles with dry, scaly skin.

options.text: A frog has dry, scaly skin, and a lizard has moist, smooth skin.
options.pick: They look alike, so they are easy to swap.
options.why: It is the other way round.

options.pick: Both are small, four-legged animals.
options.why: A frog's skin is moist and smooth.

options.pick: Both are found in gardens after rain.
options.why: A lizard's skin is dry and scaly.

title: Mould on bread
stem:
Fuzzy mould grows on an old slice of bread.

What is the mould?
key: Mould is a fungus, a living thing.

options.pick: Mould is one of the fungi named in the syllabus.
options.why: Mould is a fungus, a living thing.

options.pick: It grows like a tiny plant.
options.why: Mould is not green and cannot make its own food. It is a fungus.

options.pick: It looks like fluff.
options.why: The mould grows and spreads. It is living.

options.pick: It makes food go bad.
options.why: We can see mould with our eyes. Bacteria are too small to see.

title: Why a mushroom is not a plant
stem: Why is a mushroom not a plant?
key: Plants are green and make their own food. Fungi cannot.

options.text: It is a plant, because it grows in the ground.
options.pick: It grows where plants grow.
options.why: Growing in the ground doesn't make it a plant.

options.text: It is a plant, because it has a stalk.
options.pick: The stalk looks like a stem.
options.why: It is a fungus with a stalk, not a plant with a stem.

options.text: It is not green and cannot make its own food.
options.pick: What can plants do that a mushroom can't?
options.why: Plants are green and make their own food. Mushrooms can't, so they are fungi.

options.text: It is a plant, because it does not move.
options.pick: Plants don't move.
options.why: Not moving doesn't make it a plant.

title: Clean-looking hands
stem:
Ravi's hands look clean.

Which statement is correct?
key: Bacteria are everywhere, and too small to see without a microscope.

options.text: There can be no bacteria on them.
options.pick: Clean-looking means nothing is there.
options.why: Bacteria are too small to see. They may still be there.

options.text: Bacteria may still be there. They are too small to see without a microscope.
options.pick: Can you see bacteria with your eyes?
options.why: Bacteria are everywhere, and too small to see without a microscope.

options.text: Bacteria live only in dirty water.
options.pick: Dirty water seems to be where germs live.
options.why: Bacteria are found everywhere.

options.text: Bacteria are not living, so it doesn't matter.
options.pick: Tiny things seem not to be alive.
options.why: Bacteria are living things.

title: A fern
stem: Which statement about a fern is correct?
key: A fern is a plant that never makes flowers.

options.text: It is not a plant, because it has no flowers.
options.pick: Plants seem to need flowers.
options.why: Ferns are plants that never make flowers.

options.text: It is a flowering plant, because it has leaves.
options.pick: Most plants with leaves seem to flower.
options.why: Ferns have leaves but never make flowers.

options.text: It is a fungus, because it grows in damp places.
options.pick: Fungi like damp places.
options.why: Ferns are green plants.

options.pick: Does a fern ever make flowers?
options.why: A fern is a plant that never makes flowers.

title: A plant with no flowers
stem: Which plant never makes flowers?
key: Ferns and mosses never make flowers.

options.pick: Which one is a non-flowering plant?
options.why: Moss never makes flowers.

options.pick: It has big leaves.
options.why: A sunflower makes a big flower.

options.pick: We see its fruit more than its flowers.
options.why: A mango tree flowers before it fruits.

options.pick: Picked at random.
options.why: A hibiscus makes large flowers.

stem:
Look at the classification chart.

Into which group does a spider (8 legs, no feathers) go?

key: Answer each question in the chart about the animal, one at a time.

options.pick: Spiders seem to be insects.
options.why: A spider has 8 legs, not 6.

options.pick: It goes past the first question.
options.why: A spider has no feathers, so it goes to C.

options.pick: Answer each question in turn: 6 legs? No. Feathers? No.
options.why: No to both questions leads to Group C.

options.text: It can't be placed, because the chart doesn't mention spiders.
options.pick: Spiders aren't named.
options.why: The chart sorts by features. Answer its questions about the spider.

title: Two groups of animals
stem:
Mei sorted some animals into two groups.

Which headings could she have used?
figure:
GroupAnimals
1cat, dog, rabbit
2hen, duck, penguin
key: Find the feature that every member of a group shares.

options.text: Group 1: lives on land · Group 2: lives in water
options.pick: Ducks and penguins swim.
options.why: Hens live on land. The groups are not split by where they live.

options.pick: Some look bigger.
options.why: A rabbit is not bigger than a penguin. Size doesn't split them.

options.text: Group 1: cannot fly · Group 2: can fly
options.pick: Birds seem to fly.
options.why: A penguin cannot fly, but it is in Group 2.

options.text: Group 1: has fur · Group 2: has feathers
options.pick: What body covering do all the animals in each group share?
options.why: Cats, dogs and rabbits have fur. Hens, ducks and penguins have feathers.
